Altered States //////////////////////////////////////

"2018 was the year that I listened to less electronic music than the 5 or so previous. Strange, considering how much of it there is clogging up the internet’s pores. I had to think hard to come up with some appropriate recommendations (outside of what I released on AST), but here they are. The future is in country."

Korea Undok Group
KUG, the mysterious label and artist(s) from Winnipeg are a continuing source of inspiration for me. This year saw great releases from Erik Tisu, Zika Boys, World Counsellor and the phenomenal Cancer Pool compilation.

Beat Detectives 
After diving into their past releases and foisting one upon the world via AST earlier in the year, Beat D’s have fast become one of my favourite global acts. The perfect balance of being able to make legit jams and also take the mickey out of the form simultaneously. 

NYPD Records Volume 2: Satoshi Nakamoto's dOPENet (NYPD Records)

Krazy, Devoted & Insane MIX 2018 (NYPD Records)

Wilted Woman - Trapezoid Trappers (Plastic Bags)
A well-fried set from WW on my pal Ren’s new label, Plastic Bags, whose whole MO is “fried”. 

Boris Barksdale - Eternal Remorse (Eye For An Eye Recordings)
High-quality electronic body music from Greece.

x.y.r. - QTT7 (Quiet Time)
Russian artist x.y.r. consistently sculpts lush synthetic environments and this long-running piece for the New York based Quiet Time tapes is no exception.  

Turner Street Sound - Bunsen Burners 12" (Butter Sessions)
Melbourne duo’s debut album offering sun-drenched dub for the smoked out set.

J. Campbell - Birthstone cassette (Vienna Press)
Refined, crisp ambient music that keeps a heart beating underneath it all. Released on what is arguably East Maitland’s best experimental label. 

Parallax Records - Under The Radar Vol. 2 Compilation
Parallax is a fantastic label run in part by one of my current fave projects (TV.OUT). This follow-up to the previous Under The Radar again shows the hotbed of activity and community in the Tel Aviv electronic underground.

Regis - Play Neutral mix cassette (Hospital Productions)
Any mix that starts with Brion Gysin spoken word and seats the Arkestra alongside Monte Cazazza is alright with me.

Bloody Fist Records

One of the labels that has had one of the biggest historical impacts on my taste, Bloody Fist really stopped existing for all intents and purposes in 2004. The Old Rope 7” series, which excavates unreleased recordings from the Fisters, continues to pound their legacy into the collective cerebrum. Starting the year with a 7” from Syndicate (rep 2299) and finishing with another from Xylocaine, two of the most important novocastrian acts to be rendered in the Steel City.

In a year when gabber (specifically The Fist) became en vogue to listen to (or at least namedrop), Bloody Fist continue to offer reminders that it was done better more than two decades ago and everyone has some study to do.

Strange, considering how much of it there is clogging up the internet’s pores. I had to think hard to come up with some appropriate recommendations (outside of what I released on AST), but here they are. The future is in country." Korea Undok Group KUG, the mysterious label and artist(s) from Winnipeg are a continuing source of inspiration for me. This year saw great releases from Erik Tisu , Zika Boys , World Counsellor and the phenomenal Cancer Pool compilation. Beat Detectives After diving into their past releases and foisting one upon the world via AST earlier in the year, Beat D’s have fast become one of my favourite global acts. The perfect balance of being able to make legit jams and also take the mickey out of the form simultaneously. NYPD Records Volume 2: Satoshi Nakamoto's dOPENet (NYPD Records) Krazy, Devoted & Insane MIX 2018 (NYPD Records) Wilted Woman - Trapezoid Trappers (Plastic Bags) A well-fried set from WW on my pal Ren’s new label, Plastic Bags, whose whole MO is “fried”. Boris Barksdale - Eternal Remorse (Eye For An Eye Recordings) High-quality electronic body music from Greece. x.y.r. - QTT7 (Quiet Time) Russian artist x.y.r. consistently sculpts lush synthetic environments and this long-running piece for the New York based Quiet Time tapes is no exception. Turner Street Sound - Bunsen Burners 12" (Butter Sessions) Melbourne duo’s debut album offering sun-drenched dub for the smoked out set. J. Campbell - Birthstone cassette (Vienna Press) Refined, crisp ambient music that keeps a heart beating underneath it all. Released on what is arguably East Maitland’s best experimental label. Parallax Records - Under The Radar Vol. 2 Compilation Parallax is a fantastic label run in part by one of my current fave projects (TV.OUT). This follow-up to the previous Under The Radar again shows the hotbed of activity and community in the Tel Aviv electronic underground. Regis - Play Neutral mix cassette (Hospital Productions) Any mix that starts with Brion Gysin spoken word and seats the Arkestra alongside Monte Cazazza is alright with me. Bloody Fist Records One of the labels that has had one of the biggest historical impacts on my taste, Bloody Fist really stopped existing for all intents and purposes in 2004. The Old Rope 7” series, which excavates unreleased recordings from the Fisters, continues to pound their legacy into the collective cerebrum. Starting the year with a 7” from Syndicate (rep 2299) and finishing with another from Xylocaine, two of the most important novocastrian acts to be rendered in the Steel City. In a year when gabber (specifically The Fist) became en vogue to listen to (or at least namedrop), Bloody Fist continue to offer reminders that it was done better more than two decades ago and everyone has some study to do. what if amnesia scanner wasn't "[a] Berlin-based music duo, performing arts group, experience design studio and production house, created by Finnish-born Ville Haimala and Martti Kalliala.

Founded in 2014, Amnesia Scanner's approach is informed by a unique perspective on technology and the way it mediates contemporary experience. System vulnerabilities, information overload and sensory excess inform their work, which has found a home in both clubs and galleries.

Building on their mixtape 'AS Live [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]' (2014), Amnesia Scanner’s critically acclaimed audio play 'Angels Rig Hook' (2015) laced a potpourri of dancefloor tactics with a machinic narrator. Their dual EPs for Young

Turks, 'AS' and 'AS Truth' (2016), distilled this immersive environment into an abrasive collection of cryptorave tools. The most striking detail of ‘Another Life' is Amnesia Scanner's use of both human and inhuman voices. The latter is provided by the latest addition to the production unit, a disembodied voice called Oracle, which represents the sentience that has emerged from Amnesia Scanner.

Oracle's vocal performance ranges from exuberant mania to anxious dread and beyond. Coupled with the pop song structures that Amnesia Scanner employs for the first time, the avant-EDM productions

of ‘Another Life’ evocatively explore a schizophrenic present marked by narratives of a slow apocalypse or salvation via technology. Indeed, the lullaby of 'AS Another Life' swings between trill hope and casual

threat, lending a precarious gait to the song's staggering rhythm. The album's first single, 'AS Chaos', is its most powerfully direct track, with Pan Daijing’s English and Mandarin vocals taking over for Oracle. At its peak intensity, as in ‘AS Faceless’, Amnesia Scanner's doombahton overheats into nu-metal-gabba.

Amnesia Scanner has presented work at art institutions such as ICA London, HKW Berlin, and the Serpentine Gallery Marathon in London. They collaborate with PWR Studio for their design and visual direction. The AS live experience is co-created with Stockholm-based Canadian designer Vincent De Belleval. When unplugged from the Amnesia Scanner stream, Haimala works as a composer and producer with a wide range of musical and visual artists, and Kalliala co-directs the think tank Nemesis..."

My list this year proved difficult to cohere into any kind of ranking or to even feel like a complete list. Life in quarantine-haze and my own workflow slowing down significantly meant experiencing more of a diffuse, tough no less intense, appreciation for a great many releases as well as exhibtions, presentations, and events of all kinds by artists that I found important at different times through the year. EVENTS

Kraak Festival 2020 with sets by Aylu, Vica Pacheco, Orphan Fairytale, Quanta Qualia, Mesías Maiguashca amongst others. It was great to work together with Lizzy Vandirendonk on the visual decor of the fest as well.

Kraak’s Spring Brakers series of virtual concerts which are still available to watch online here:
https://vimeo.com/user50024974

All editions of Musa Ullakolla on SWGBO (a cracked version of finish virtual social platform Habbo Hotel). These events were important in reaffirming the connectedness between freaks from the experimental music scenes of Finland, Belgium, USA, and beyond during the dark times of pandemic isolation. Held by the wonderful Suomi elves Samuli Tanner and Heta Bilaletdin. Insane allstar lineups!
Here a video from Kuupuu’s new record, featuring scenes from her concert in the venue where this all took place:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Um3RxrJ4fbw

Samuli’s and Heta’s concerts in our house in the beginning of the year were also major highlights, here an excerpt of Tanner’s game:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WDTnbZI4p3M

Clarice Calvo-Pinsolle’s (aka Lamina) brain melting set @ Q-O2
(Look for her music in one of the releases on KRUT along two other grand high witches, and in the sound sorcery episode of Spring Brakers < ; ^ )

Roxane Métayer & Kaito’s concert on a boat under a bridge in the outskirts of Brussels to the backdrop of a setting sun reflecting pink on the rippling canal and a puffin nuclear plant styled chimney.

Dreamy Timidi’s concert in the oh so magickal closing night of Nuova Atlantide.

Playing a hidden concert with my hermanos Ernesto Gonzalez (Bear Bones Lay Low), Tony Marie (Loto Retina) and Daniel Dariel 

Screening of Henri Michaux’s psychedelic films @ Cinematek Brussels. One of the most visually accurate representations of these mental states that I’ve seen.

MOVIES

Milieu - Damien Faure
Beautiful documentary on the life of people in relation to their environment on a small Japanese island regularly hit by typhoons. A lovely example of life in a slow rhythm with reverence for the unspeakable, sometimes represented as spirits. Great soundtrack sets the tone without imposing itself on the “silence” of “nature”.

Split - Chris Shaw
Mind boggling hidden gem of independent Gringo Sci-fi, a story about a guy in his struggle against Control and Order armed with a mysterious substance that sets your mind free. Funky visual effects and sampledelic soundtrack that sounds like it could have been made by Spencer Clark. Smash the Apollonian shell and let Chaos pour through the cracks!

Habitat - René Daalder
In a post apocalyptic world, where your skin boils if exposed to the unfiltered solar radiation, an outlandish family turns the outside-in by making their house into a living environment and “giving evolution a kick in the butt”. Deep and unlikely treatment of the genre (William Blake quote included ;)

Gremlins 2: The New Batch
Rewatched this childhood classic and was very pleasantly surprised. A clever critique on capitalism and surveillance society. Packed with meta-meta jokes on Hollywood culture. It even laughs at the now very familiar trend of “green” capitalism. Still relevant!

GAMES 

Myst III: Exile
The gameplay might not be the most fluent, considering it’s point and click, but the futuristic-elven-art-nouveau-punk aesthetics, the trippy ambient soundtrack, the challenging and sophisticated mind game puzzles and the fact that it all takes place in worlds that are books, where a character messes things up to take revenge on their writter/creator, all make it a great piece of art to me. Wish I could live in there, at least while the plague is here.

Primordial Void ///////////////////////////

“Easy Way” by Surface to Air Missive is my favorite song of 2020. The harmonies on this track are to die for. The whole thing is like a dream. Frontman Taylor Ross reminds me a lot of Alex Chilton; both are charming Southern boys with highly distinctive vocal and songwriting styles. Surface to Air Missive are quite possibly the best thing to come out of Athens since R.E.M./Love Tractor.

Along with “Easy Way,” I also enjoyed Legio X’s 19 Quarantine Beats and Mark Kozelek’s All the Best, Isaac Hayes. Truth be told, I didn’t listen to a whole lot of music from this year that wasn’t released on Primordial Void. 

2020 has been a horrible, confusing mess. I have music and my dearest friends to thank for helping me get through this tough year.

BOOKS Alina Popa - Square of Will in Square of Love Alina Popa & Florin Flueras - Unsorcery Clarice Lispector - The Passion According to G.H. CCRU - Writings 1997 - 2003 Vilém Flusser - Vampyrotheutis Infernalis Caetano Veloso - Tropical Truth MOVIES Milieu - Damien Faure Beautiful documentary on the life of people in relation to their environment on a small Japanese island regularly hit by typhoons. A lovely example of life in a slow rhythm with reverence for the unspeakable, sometimes represented as spirits. Great soundtrack sets the tone without imposing itself on the “silence” of “nature”. Split - Chris Shaw Mind boggling hidden gem of independent Gringo Sci-fi, a story about a guy in his struggle against Control and Order armed with a mysterious substance that sets your mind free. Funky visual effects and sampledelic soundtrack that sounds like it could have been made by Spencer Clark. Smash the Apollonian shell and let Chaos pour through the cracks! Habitat - René Daalder In a post apocalyptic world, where your skin boils if exposed to the unfiltered solar radiation, an outlandish family turns the outside-in by making their house into a living environment and “giving evolution a kick in the butt”. Deep and unlikely treatment of the genre (William Blake quote included ;) Gremlins 2: The New Batch Rewatched this childhood classic and was very pleasantly surprised. A clever critique on capitalism and surveillance society. Packed with meta-meta jokes on Hollywood culture. It even laughs at the now very familiar trend of “green” capitalism. Still relevant! GAMES Myst III: Exile The gameplay might not be the most fluent, considering it’s point and click, but the futuristic-elven-art-nouveau-punk aesthetics, the trippy ambient soundtrack, the challenging and sophisticated mind game puzzles and the fact that it all takes place in worlds that are books, where a character messes things up to take revenge on their writter/creator, all make it a great piece of art to me. Wish I could live in there, at least while the plague is here. Gibby:

Alex G - God Save the Animals (Domino Recording Co Ltd.)

incredible music by songwriting mastermind Alex G and wow what an incredible producer he has proven to be again.
Love where he's going and so excited for what's more to come. Bless his soul.
Will see him playing live for the first time in 2023 and I'm beyond excited. probably my fav album of 2022.

Chris Olsen - Human! Sound! —> & or the record i could never finish )Van Dank)

lovely playful music that really feels comforting to me yet written very intelligently.
love the many layers the production has especially the vocals. also, the last song "Her Notebook" is stunning.
also big fan and supporter of Van Dank, the selection has always been very strong and personal. I'm very excited for things to come.

lighyer - Wongk Dust (2019-2022) [summon] (album visualizer)

this was actually a modem discovery for me! So thanks Matej ;o)
I really love the sound quality of this album, it gives low fidelity sampler vibes and it's very inspiring to see how certain samples are repeated and mangled together
I especially like "I was wrong". love the uncanny feeling you get from the time measure being all twisted yet there's repetition and it feels very intimate and melancholic. good title.

RLX ASSASSYN - Lost Since We Started Following Insects into the Woods (MIND CLUB)

this release opened 2022 so well. I mean, all-round amazing production: consistent yet always original. Always impressed by rlx assassyn.

claire rousay - it was always worth it / ilysm (Mended Dreams)

this is technically a late 2021 album, but I had to include it because it has been so influential for my work this year.
wonderful combination of field recording, synths and spokenword.it feels like a collage of many things, listening to this is like listening to a story. love claire rousay!

FLAG21 - I've been covering this collective (on LaidOffNYC's now deceased monthly column RIP) since the pandemic and they keep getting better and better. On a trip to Tokyo this fall, Riona and I met up with NowLedge and his energy is as great in person as it is in his music. He recommended going to KATO MASSACRE, a weekly Wednesday night party held at FORESTLIMIT, and we lucked into the 400th anniversary party. I don't say this lightly, it was the most life affirming musical experience I've attended. As Nowledge put it: it is "Tokyo's purest party." Between visiting the Island of Enoshima for guerilla street performances in the underpass of a bridge on the Pacific Ocean to 8 hours of passionate, music-obsessed DJs and performers covering, quite possibly, every musical genre in one day at OPPA-LA, MASSACRE is a mega-vibe.

records.title: Best labels of 2023
records.bodyHtml:
★ 19 labels in alphabetical order and 19 of their best-of lists in no particular order★

ArachHE ///////

Experiences:

Narthex Festival
Run, and populated, by the most beautiful souls. Shoutout to the Nutria of the pond for maintaining its peace throughout. Narthex Forever!

Geomantic Journeying with White Goblin, via the living time portal of Butser Ancient Farm, through the ritual landscapes and sacred springs of the South West of England, to the Neolithic facehugger tomb of Belas Knap in Gloucestershire. 

Petronn Sphene live @ Wharf Chambers. Total cathartic neural exploding-head-syndrome blasts expelling all internal cobwebs into the Oort Cloud. 

Limpe Fuchs live in the Blue John-encrusted chambers of Treak Cliff Cavern, in Castleton, Derbyshire. Highlight was the moment she bade some attendants to place copper drums beneath the constant drips, and said “now, we can listen to the cave” and after thereby having lulled the audience, who were turned away from the stage now, snuck out a wooden horn and uttered loud troll parps over our heads. A truer witch, I do not know! 

Discovering the nearby, exposed, Carboniferous reef of Chrome Hill aka Dragon’s Back Ridge (replete with its amazing number of Gigantoproductus and crinoid fossils) with good friends ready to sit and rifle through rocks for some time before slipping gracelessly down the slick limestone and clay-mud sides of the submerged petrified cryptid. 

Listening to Steve Reich - Tehillim while flying over ever-changing clouds from NL to UK, staring out the window 100% of the journey. 

Leaving a hellish teaching job, having more time to play shows (alone and in groups), thus meeting and connecting with many people and gradually reawakening to my truer self.

 Artetetra Bugtech Petting Zoo Gin&Platonic Hyperlink Kumo Communication Nonlocal Research Mappa EXILES Orange Milk Ukiuki Atama IW katharsis 111records ArachHE Pampsychia Cime i.u Quantum Natives Clam 
 ★ 19 labels in alphabetical order and 19 of their best-of lists in no particular order★ ArachHE /////// Experiences: Narthex Festival Run, and populated, by the most beautiful souls. Shoutout to the Nutria of the pond for maintaining its peace throughout. Narthex Forever! Geomantic Journeying with White Goblin, via the living time portal of Butser Ancient Farm, through the ritual landscapes and sacred springs of the South West of England, to the Neolithic facehugger tomb of Belas Knap in Gloucestershire. Petronn Sphene live @ Wharf Chambers. Total cathartic neural exploding-head-syndrome blasts expelling all internal cobwebs into the Oort Cloud. Limpe Fuchs live in the Blue John-encrusted chambers of Treak Cliff Cavern, in Castleton, Derbyshire. Highlight was the moment she bade some attendants to place copper drums beneath the constant drips, and said “now, we can listen to the cave” and after thereby having lulled the audience, who were turned away from the stage now, snuck out a wooden horn and uttered loud troll parps over our heads. A truer witch, I do not know! Discovering the nearby, exposed, Carboniferous reef of Chrome Hill aka Dragon’s Back Ridge (replete with its amazing number of Gigantoproductus and crinoid fossils) with good friends ready to sit and rifle through rocks for some time before slipping gracelessly down the slick limestone and clay-mud sides of the submerged petrified cryptid. Listening to Steve Reich - Tehillim while flying over ever-changing clouds from NL to UK, staring out the window 100% of the journey. Leaving a hellish teaching job, having more time to play shows (alone and in groups), thus meeting and connecting with many people and gradually reawakening to my truer self. Domi:

WTRGRL - Dripsody (self-released) (such a nice release with intriguing sound design - something inbetween mainstream and underground sounds)

Iglooghost - Tidal Memory Exo (LUCKYME) (one of my most listened albums this year, i really admire the narrative aspect of the whole record. when i was in athents treating this LP like my ost to traveling by metro, i was astonished of how well it incorporates the fragile fossil-like qualities into an amazing digital and dirty soundscapes)

NEW YORK - RAPSTAR (Relaxin) (just feeling like taking it for a walk in a big city vibe... very poetic, and soft

Babii - DareDevil2000 (BOXSET) (such a nice record, surprising with production on every step - and the artists vocals are so on point)

Death's Dynamic Shroud and Galen Tipton - You Like Music (Ghost Diamond) (post-techno, post-club, post-music hymn of digital anarchism. i think the names capture the approach of the artists to this lp. it is breaking your expectations and surprising u on every step. i really love music... )

Julek:

【 1-Fav Movie 】’Vulcanizadora’ dir Joel Potrykus beautiful, intimate meta-sequel to all of the previous slackery-grotesque junk-food-incel-stories from Joel. just plz don’t get fooled by tags - it’s not a horror flick at all . it’s a very descriptive movie about suicide 

【 2-Fav Yt Video ! 】’Why YouTube Thumbnails Matter’ by ThorHighHeels Thor might be my fav youtuber ( or maybe i should call them ToiTube Artiste ) right now . their multi-level-meta-wordplay is a wild ride through childishly unpretentious syllabic repetitions and exquisite vulgarity. hmm they just have this very distinct melody to their narration… also, this very particular vid im talking about could totally be a short movie by mid 2010s Jon Rafman or smth like that ! Thor’s visual universe is truly one of a kind 

【 3-Fav Soundcloud Rmx / MashUp 】’Gucci Flip Flops On Einstein Beach’ by 250666 opera trilogy by Philip Glass might be one of the best trilogies ever made – it makes me cry , it makes me feel uplifted , it makes me feel free for a moment and it finally makes me fall down on my knees . so happy that someone [ Gibby(-Dj) Forever ! ]) finally did The Ultimate Justice to the beautiful melancholic gucci ballad by Bhad Bhabie mashing it up with The Ultimate Opera experience . made me spill a tear once or twice ps shut out to Apu Nanu who made my 2nd fav remix of the year by upgrading ‚Hi Bitch’ also by Bhabie 

【 4-Fav Music album 】Not Possible To Choose Just One ( feel like each below shaped me a little and all of them are lil masterpieces )

joe hisaishi—joe hisaishi in vienna

Another great year for Musick! 

Piia Rinne - River Eye (Artsy) 

Piia Rinne uses tape and sampler, arranging sounds with the radicallity of a child at play, free and easy. Suomi seal of certification, and also coming from artsy, you know it’s ill. 

matt robidoux - m e s h s o n g s ep (self-released) 

Elegant tripping balls. 

v.a. - Musique Muscle #22 (Musique Muscle) 

Don’t mind being trapped in this labyrinth for a while. Nice twists and turns on Brussels based Musique Muscle 

Nuke Watch - Worlds Gone M.A.D. (The Trilogy Tapes)

Nuke Watch - Pepper's Ghost (Patience / Impatience) 

MARILIZE LEGUANA. Some of the sickest jams alive. Chris Hontos and Aaron Anderson I detect a beat are joined by Chris Farstad (Galaxy Express 555) William Statler (Free Music) and Cole Pulice amongst others. 

Horace Manucace - Emanuelle Augustus (yé,fra!) 

Swag as it gets, our boy Loïc strikes again and again. Reinventing the love song, free, large and fresh. 

v.a. - âtre1 (yé,fra!) 

Dope compilation of mainly French artists in benefit for Palestine, support and get amazing contemporary sounds in return. 

BICCO BEAT - BICCO BEAT (Biome) 

Eclectic and cute song vignettes from a Japanese one man band. Lovely artwork by the one and only Eric Kinny. Can’t go wrong with Biome. 

LIFEPOD5 - The Bravest Selfie Ever (Clam) 

Apparently if you take a selfie of your brain in this day and age it sounds like this 

Kuthi Jin & Talpah - Skurnakkiat (Clam) 

Bouncy harsh is not dead! 

Gilles Poizat - Trouvé perdu (La République des Granges) 

Nice mix of modular synth, bugle ala Hassell, and voice with a French touch. Beautiful and strange songs, where the voice and bugle interact with the synths, in great symbiosis of human and machine. Folk of now, music to fly and to dance. 

Aymeric de Tapol - Aiguillage (La République des Granges) 

Brussels based rhythmic synth maestro. Maybe it’s just me but I get some Residents vibes at times on this one, which is of course a good thing. 

Tutoriel - Innocent Tools (Bidule)

Tutoriel - pelican school (self-released) 

Double Tutoriel so you can learn what a midi tutorial sounds like in French. It’s more fun than you can imagine. 1/2 of the fantastic Elastic Systems. Thanks for making us dance this year! 

Nicolas Gaunin - Huti ケ​゙​ー​ム (Artetetra) 

More plastic sounding than the rest of his work, but we’ve developed the ability to digest plastic, so YUMMA. It’s not difficult to make a parallel to the two albums above by Tutoriel, even the covers correspond with each other. I’m pretty sure this is just a “belle coïncidence”. 

Tomutonttu - Halki pilvien (Edições CN) 

Through the clouds, this Finnish dust gnome delivers. Jan never failed us. 

v.a. - Bag of Toys 2 (modem) 

Wish we could have been on this superb comp, Matej Kart All-stars. Many friends and favourite artists (which are often both) 

TOMÉ - pinch (surf) 

Surf’s up 

Everything by Csocsó. The defiance and definition of new weird electronic music. For androids and humans alike. 

Melon Musk - Né sous X (fals.ch) 

Dystopian lullabies for altered states, disturbing, soothing, alienating and comforting. 

Elledans Bruskhat - Fairy Music 1 (Stenze Quo) 

music recorded on Samså, Denmark. Looking forward to a full length album! 

Aloe Static - Aloe Static (self-released) 

Always a fan of Luke Thinnes, here he is together with Andrew Dahabrah concocting this delicious aloe brew, refreshing and healing. 

estuary..fragmentation:.,. ‘ ,’. ,., . ,’ . ,’ . - shattered tissue recomposition​.​•​°​•​. (self-released) 

Avant phone music from Denver, Colorado. There seems to be something in the water over there, wanna taste. 

Alto Fuero - Live Rec (self-released) 

Loto Retina and Victoria Palacios, selected sound recordings. Do I need to say more? I won’t. 

Darrell DeVore - Another Song of Civilization (Goaty Tapes / House Rules) 

Sound magic from Pygmy Unit’s Darrell DeVore, what a beauty! 

Frituuur Aconcagua - Frituuur Aconcagua (KRAAK) 

Transatlantic trio of Nicolás Carcavilla (Embassador Dulgoon), David Jarrín (Dispocisión Asoleada) y Pablo Pico (Bardo Todol). South meets North and old meets new. Deeply fried and friedly deep. 

guervens - college dropout (Ukiuki Atama) 

Those mischievous little demons inside your phone dropped out of college and are having a party remixing your data 

Cahn Ingold Prelog - The Well​-​Tempered Diffusion Model (wabi-sabi) 

An AI trained on many spectrograms of music is taught how different music looks like. Based on this knowledge it is prompted to interpret the titles of the first 13 parts of Bach’s The Well-Tempered Clavier. The resulting Midi compositions are then orchestrated by the human artist. 

Señor Service - Envisioned Homesickness (Riforma) 

Our dearest real bwoy sublimated his broken heart into these sweet love songs. Best enjoyed on your own 

sofi - AZE (Riforma) 

Haven’t heard this one much yet but I like the feel of these critters crawling around in my brain. 

linUSB - Mouth Sounds (self-released) 

Party in a mouth, vowels and consonants can be so much fun. 

{scope} - Nightcap (Kohlhaas) 

Free Jazz is today years old, alive and well as yung Marshall Allen Double trouble from Nante’s Jean Turner 

Matière Danse - Le Cabaret et le Printemps (self-released) 

Fonky wonky musick, get down with it! 

Abstraction Mathématique - Des Maths (self-released) 

Extra wacky. Also check Jean’s visual wonder world : @jean__turner 

Kalozin - Prakatun (Kinship) 

Kalozin explores the possibilities of stretching and twisting an array of sounds from the rich acoustic palette of Brazil in simultaneously slow and fast tempo. Another golazo from this incredible artist. 

Matteo Coffetti - Cave Kids Exploration (IW) 

Adventurous parties in caves with the friends, elves and goblins alike. Bombastik.

Bruno stayed at our house a bit a couple of years back, from what I could tell he is a non-conformist, committed to push his music making out of comfort and the known. Please keep going. 

Polonius - Polonius (Stoned To Death) 

Tricks out of a hat, steam from a half opened manhole cover, glimmers in the alleyway, the sound of a bowling ball hitting a strike.

Very enjoyable guitar grooves and voicemail messages.

Absolute banger of speed merengue by Dj Roadrunner on Cartajena Ink from Valparaiso, Chile. Llamen a los bomberes, la pista de baile arde!

galen tipton - clean dreams (self-released) 

Dear Galen, keep dreaming 4ever  

Augustė Vickunaitė - DANCE ALONE (self-released) 

Lithuanian sorceress prepares pulsating sonic concoctions, using tape as sound matter and tape machines as instruments, warping the sounds physically and incorporating the cyclic noises and mechanisms of the tape players themselves. There’s a strange sense of groove, maybe it’s the insistence of the loops, but I have the tendency to bounce my head or rock my body as if I would be listening to Hip-Hop. 

Rébecca Bonté - Noli Me Tangere (Tanzprocesz) 

1/2 of Acte Bonte, Rebecca casts a spell with her voice over industrial sounding electronics, concrete music and downtempo beats weaving entrancing rhythm-based compositions with oddly pleasing melodies. 

SUN ARAW - Lifetime (Drag City) 

A master lays it down. Even groovier and more hard hitting than ever. Years of experience applied. A lifetime is a lifetime no matter how long. 

Nitty Sun Trick - computer water games (Pho Bho) 

The concert that this is the recording of was a highlight of A.R.X. (already a highlight in itself) last year. Is this a soup-a-groop?

Fifth World representatives on French label Bamboo Shows. Some hard neo-free-exotica on these 2 side long tracks. 

id m theft able - Tambourine Green (self-released) 

Shuffled rearrangements of classic hits on 7 inch, by quartering and gluing them back together. This master of collage in every possible expression of the term goes on and on. Also check @idmtheftable for more audiovisual fun. 

Kim David Bots & Lyckle de Jong - the third of may (South of North) 

Dreamy soundtrack to an imagined story (printed on the LP cover) about a close encounter of some kind, with a creature that projects the past of Den Helder, a town in the north of Holland that is the most bombed city in the Netherlands, in the mind of J. the protagonist. 

Roy Werner - Imagine My Surprise (Moon Glyph) 

Imagine our surprise hearing this, knowing G.S Sultan. Stunningly beautiful. Featuring, among others, Baptiste Martin (Les Halles) 

Robert Schwarz - Stridulations 1-14 (Superpang) 

Those lovely neuron picking electronic sounds. 

Lee Evans - Dream Logic (self-released) 

Trippy organic modular polyrhythmics 

Harry Gorski-Brown - Durt Dronemaker After Dreamboats (GLARC) 

I just love em’ bagpipes. 

Nicolás Carcavilla - The Last Servants (Embassador Dulgoon) 

This is an audio movie, an opera prima. Maybe it’s a perceptual hologram beamed into your mind by the sounds of the Embassador and the voice of Kenneth Welsh! (Habitat, Twin Peaks). Performed by the man before he left us in 2022. May your consciousness find a better fate than that of the character you played here, an AI wandering and wondering, lost and alone in the bleak landscape of Antartica. 

loto retina - winter improzzz (self-released) 

Who needs Santa? Loto returns from noodle galaxy just in time to gift us with these jamz, these gemz to help us through the winter window. See you on the other side! 

Inner Cop Avoidance - Inner Cop Avoidance (iriai verlag) 

Jam band from Köln featuring our pal Seb (Hipólito) on drums and percussion. First and last tracks reminds me of La Banda’s, very repetitive and meditative playing, warping time n’ space, The second track is a spoken first person narration over a melting gamelan. Sweeeta 

Tabloid - Bag to Bag (iriai verlag) 

Another excellent release on Iriai Verlag, a mental sound walk. “Like trekking through the alps with François Bayle” says Sebastian von Der Heide. 

ALEPHER - Dodges Aim (self-released) 

Huge collection of blunted slow burners from Trii related group. Exquisite FM tones and textures with smooth n’ stylish polyrhythms. 

hoen - 方縁 2017 (Kumo Communication) 

2017 vintage archives from hoen : ] Kinda minimal, at times almost drill or trap instrumentals, with the eeriness of an absence of the characteristically human, the voice. Sometimes they feel like AI reimaginations of contemporary pop music, or if not AI maybe Asmus Tietschens 

seaketa - SoundCloud Archives 2017​-​2021 (Kumo Communication) 

Seaketa’s Soundcloud archives collected in one place for convenience. 

ap​ö​pa - kiri pati (tissue★box & ASC)

ap​ö​pa - bala atap (tissue★box & ASC) 

Loopy, bouncy, punchy, loosey goosey, squishy, squeaky, wonky, fonky, blinkity blopy. Wackyness of the finest quality, Japanese. 

Books: 

Read lot’s of Philip K. Dick this and last year. It does add an extra layer to the reading that so much of the world he describes, technologies and ways of employing them echo so much our own world and time. The way in which he predicted the intrusion (and by now near omnipresence) of computers into our lives, the rise of AI, and of Mars as a new frontier of capitalism is uncanny. Including unsettling and deep philosophical/spiritual explorations about the nature of reality and what it means to be human. After several novels I start feeling a bit like some of his characters, or as he felt, a character dreamed by a mind in the greater poly-novel of existence. 

Films/Videos: 

Beyond the infinite two minutes It’s rare that a movie will blow my mind so much. This is a hilarious, mind boggling, intelligent as fuck, economic, unpretentious, sci-fi without special effects, flawless single shot movie. Good idea, great script, incredible film. As Eric Kinny said: “Note to past self: go watch this movie!” 

The Cosmic Eye Thoughtful “children’s” animation, with a one-world discourse. 

Breakfast of Champions Kinny recommendation, thnx! Easily Bruce Willis finest moment. As daring as a Hollywood movie is allowed to be I guess, those days are long gone though, big data analysis rules the game, no more risk taking, just crowd pleasing. 

Hellzapoppin’ Yet another Kinny tip. Insane meta-cinema from 1941! They don’t miss a gag. 

Mandala and The Clay Peacock by Art Clokey Mostly known as the creator of Gumbo, this guy tripped ballsack and here’s the proof. Pure magic. 

Happy Fuji News by Eric Kinny Who says you need 24 frames per second? Sans Soleil already taught us differently. I saw this movie twice this year having already seen it once last year, I’m still not bored of it. This amazing woodcut feature film is another proof that you don’t need much more than good use of the old noodle to make excellent cinema. Eric has made 200 woodcut “slides” that he (or another “projectionist”) makes pass through a wooden frame, synced to the audio track which consists of the voices of the characters (Siet Rae, Mcloud Zicmuse amongst many others) and music by Raphael Desmarets. Funny, beautiful and moving. Go watch this if you can, and if it’s not playing somewhere near you, book him! He plays living rooms (Now also in Japanese ; ) Learn more: @eric_kinny Booking: @email 

Videoclip for Ikue Mori & Charmaine Lee - Royal Flush Made by the fantastic Anibal Bley, top-o-classo animator per excellence, if your eyes haven’t had the pleasure to meet Anibal’s work, let me be their cupid https://www.youtube.com/@AnibalBley. He is also an incredible musician, Lavina Yelb being the moniker for the audio side of this diamond. Please treat yourself. 

So many amazing concerts and arts this year that it gets hard to mention and say something about them all. 

I have to mention one because it moved me very deeply. Also not really a concert, but the wildest puppet theater performance. 

Poncilli Creacion (w/ live music by Kuthi Jin) @ the container in Berlin. These Boricua twins made my heart and mind explode. Goosbumps,laughter and tears. It spoke one message loudly - if you do something you love, give it all! @poncilicreacion 

Thanks to everyone putting their whole being into what they do, with love and hope. Let’s keep making it worthwhile and keep our communities alive and growing. Much love

ALEPHER - Dodges Aim (self-released) Huge collection of blunted slow burners from Trii related group. Exquisite FM tones and textures with smooth n’ stylish polyrhythms. hoen - 方縁 2017 (Kumo Communication) 2017 vintage archives from hoen : ] Kinda minimal, at times almost drill or trap instrumentals, with the eeriness of an absence of the characteristically human, the voice. Sometimes they feel like AI reimaginations of contemporary pop music, or if not AI maybe Asmus Tietschens seaketa - SoundCloud Archives 2017​-​2021 (Kumo Communication) Seaketa’s Soundcloud archives collected in one place for convenience. ap​ö​pa - kiri pati (tissue★box & ASC) ap​ö​pa - bala atap (tissue★box & ASC) Loopy, bouncy, punchy, loosey goosey, squishy, squeaky, wonky, fonky, blinkity blopy. Wackyness of the finest quality, Japanese. Books: Read lot’s of Philip K. Dick this and last year. It does add an extra layer to the reading that so much of the world he describes, technologies and ways of employing them echo so much our own world and time. The way in which he predicted the intrusion (and by now near omnipresence) of computers into our lives, the rise of AI, and of Mars as a new frontier of capitalism is uncanny. Including unsettling and deep philosophical/spiritual explorations about the nature of reality and what it means to be human. After several novels I start feeling a bit like some of his characters, or as he felt, a character dreamed by a mind in the greater poly-novel of existence. Films/Videos: Beyond the infinite two minutes It’s rare that a movie will blow my mind so much. This is a hilarious, mind boggling, intelligent as fuck, economic, unpretentious, sci-fi without special effects, flawless single shot movie. Good idea, great script, incredible film. As Eric Kinny said: “Note to past self: go watch this movie!” The Cosmic Eye Thoughtful “children’s” animation, with a one-world discourse. Breakfast of Champions Kinny recommendation, thnx! Easily Bruce Willis finest moment. As daring as a Hollywood movie is allowed to be I guess, those days are long gone though, big data analysis rules the game, no more risk taking, just crowd pleasing. Hellzapoppin’ Yet another Kinny tip. Insane meta-cinema from 1941! They don’t miss a gag. Mandala and The Clay Peacock by Art Clokey Mostly known as the creator of Gumbo, this guy tripped ballsack and here’s the proof. Pure magic. Happy Fuji News by Eric Kinny Who says you need 24 frames per second? Sans Soleil already taught us differently. I saw this movie twice this year having already seen it once last year, I’m still not bored of it. This amazing woodcut feature film is another proof that you don’t need much more than good use of the old noodle to make excellent cinema. Eric has made 200 woodcut “slides” that he (or another “projectionist”) makes pass through a wooden frame, synced to the audio track which consists of the voices of the characters (Siet Rae, Mcloud Zicmuse amongst many others) and music by Raphael Desmarets. Funny, beautiful and moving. Go watch this if you can, and if it’s not playing somewhere near you, book him! He plays living rooms (Now also in Japanese ; ) Learn more: @eric_kinny Booking: @email Videoclip for Ikue Mori & Charmaine Lee - Royal Flush Made by the fantastic Anibal Bley, top-o-classo animator per excellence, if your eyes haven’t had the pleasure to meet Anibal’s work, let me be their cupid https://www.youtube.com/@AnibalBley . He is also an incredible musician, Lavina Yelb being the moniker for the audio side of this diamond. Please treat yourself. So many amazing concerts and arts this year that it gets hard to mention and say something about them all. I have to mention one because it moved me very deeply. Also not really a concert, but the wildest puppet theater performance. Poncilli Creacion (w/ live music by Kuthi Jin) @ the container in Berlin. These Boricua twins made my heart and mind explode. Goosbumps,laughter and tears. It spoke one message loudly - if you do something you love, give it all! @poncilicreacion Thanks to everyone putting their whole being into what they do, with love and hope. Let’s keep making it worthwhile and keep our communities alive and growing. Beat Concern //////////////////////////

Retrograde Youth - We're Not Humans Anymore (Pinkman Records)

This is both my top 12" and label of 2017. Pinkman has smashed it consistently to the point where I feel I could blind order anything they release. It's an aspirational meter for a labels quality. Of all the 12"s which includes Das Ding, Indentified Patient and Palmbomben II, it was Retrograde Youth that took the title. I saw Lena Wilikens drop this in Corsica Studios last week and it was a perfect dance floor moment.

Timeron - Nice Trainers Acid (Acid Waxa)

Timeron has created pure joy with a 303. I love acid and new ways of improving it are few and far between, but this track hit instant repeat and is a giant step from his previous cassette on Where To Now?.

Assel - This Will Not Stand (Where To Now?)

WTN are always on the money with the best challenging electronic music. Assel was a slow burner for me, but after coming back from a long night dancing, this clicked with me at 7am on a sunday morning and stayed in my record pile nearest to my decks since.

Desert Peace - Placeholder for a Palace (upcoming on Total Black)

I've been really lucky to start my label Beat Concern with 2 x 12"s for my favourite artists from Australia Roman Nails and Collector (and there are tons more I love and coming soon on BC I hope). The two of them got together and recorded this cassette of eerie synths, drones, found sounds and industrial leanings and it kills.

Rings Around Saturn - Unthank 11 (Unthank / Firecracker Records)

Another Australian pick, this time on the Firecracker sub label Unthank that has the most beautiful screen printed covers like its parent label. These labels are worth collecting as bits of art, luckily the sounds contained within are 100% gold. This 10" and 7" combo gets more listens than I would normally afford other records across multi format releases.

Lost Angles ////////////////////////////////

Vektroid - Seed and Synthetic Earth (self-released)

This record is fantastic in many ways, from the wild SoundBlaster style instrumentation to the wealth of melodies and genuinely catchy songs, Vektroid once again paves new ground for her ever-evolving style of music.

Machine Girl - ...BECAUSE I'M YOUNG AND ARROGANT AND HATE EVERYTHING YOU STAND FOR (Orange Milk)

This record is as unwieldy as it is brilliant. Hyper beats with hyper music for hyper people, the untamed ferocity is super admirable and you just can't hate it. Music to throw chairs to!

BARCHboi - Keyboard_SHAREWARE.midi (business casual)

A very beautiful and well composed album with the added twist of these laughably corny midi stock sounds that just make for the best juxtaposition of impressive songwriting and absurd tonal choices. The silliness balances out the work and it just ends up being a great record.

Kagami Smile - Thigh (BLCR Laboratories)

From the creepy surreal Shintaro Kago-esque artwork to the hi-fi granular rhythms and sounds, this album is really a fantastic listen. Much more laidback than Kagami Smile's typical sound, this felt more focused and utilized chaotic ideas in a more structured way. It'll please anybody looking for more organic sounds congealed around the skeleton of a contemporary beat-driven piece.

FIRE-TOOLZ - INTERBEING (Bedlam Tapes)

Combing my two loves, Industrial music and vaporwave, into a lovely mess of vapornoise textures, FIRE-TOOLZ hits back with yet another flamethrower. I greatly admire her curation with Swamp Circle records but her sound is near-unmatched in the (imo) under-appreciated subgenre of vaporwave.

Pharmakon - Contact (Sacred Bones)

One of the most powerful presences in the industrial and harsh noise scenes, Pharmakon never fails to please with her screeching steel and unhindered ferocity. This record is just so vicious, with its sheer hatred burning through just as strong as ever. 

ZONΞ ΞATΞR vs. §E▲ ▓F D▓G§ (Chamber38)

This is probably the most insane mixture of sampled industrial and noise metal I've ever heard. Like a thousand saw blades in a vortex of distorted guitars, blast beats, death growls, power electronics. The list goes one, but its safe to say this masterpiece is a fantastic aural cleanser. 

Tee Lopes - Sonic Mania OST (Data Discs)

What else can I say that hasn't already been established? The Sonic franchise has the best music and its just as good as ever with the addition of new classics like Studiopolis and Press Garden.

LEUCROCUTA - when all the animals are dead (self-release)

A jarring and beautiful soundtrack to the sci-fi dystopic world beyond nature. The concept is strong enough alone, but the music holds up just as well, pressing some lovely synth-waves sounds harshened by the banshee-esque shrieked vocal performance that adds a fantastic spice to the dissonant danceable sounds.

VRTUA - LOUD FORMATIONS (Beer on the Rug)

That Yamaha chip is just the most unbeatable sound around. FM was damn near perfected by the Sega Genesis' sound engine and this masterpiece is living proof. Using the sounds from said chip, VTRUA harnesses the limitations to breed this fantastic showcase of what you can do marrying todays techniques with yesterday's killer sounds.

WULFFLUW XCIV - LosSantos Club Riddim (YOUNG VIBEZ) (We would say that every single track by WULFFLUW has to be mentioned but especially this one was essential) HDMIRROR - Embody EP (JEROME) 111X - Authority (self-released) DJ Smokey 666 - Positive Squad The Soundtrack Vol. 1 (self-released) CELES7E - From Ashes (Symbols) Bulma - Crime Scene (Symbols) Beat Concern /////// // /////// /// /////// Retrograde Youth - We're Not Humans Anymore (Pinkman Records) This is both my top 12" and label of 2017. Pinkman has smashed it consistently to the point where I feel I could blind order anything they release. It's an aspirational meter for a labels quality. Of all the 12"s which includes Das Ding, Indentified Patient and Palmbomben II, it was Retrograde Youth that took the title. I saw Lena Wilikens drop this in Corsica Studios last week and it was a perfect dance floor moment. Timeron - Nice Trainers Acid (Acid Waxa) Timeron has created pure joy with a 303. I love acid and new ways of improving it are few and far between, but this track hit instant repeat and is a giant step from his previous cassette on Where To Now?. Assel - This Will Not Stand (Where To Now?) WTN are always on the money with the best challenging electronic music. Assel was a slow burner for me, but after coming back from a long night dancing, this clicked with me at 7am on a sunday morning and stayed in my record pile nearest to my decks since. Desert Peace - Placeholder for a Palace (upcoming on Total Black) I've been really lucky to start my label Beat Concern with 2 x 12"s for my favourite artists from Australia Roman Nails and Collector (and there are tons more I love and coming soon on BC I hope). The two of them got together and recorded this cassette of eerie synths, drones, found sounds and industrial leanings and it kills. Rings Around Saturn - Unthank 11 (Unthank / Firecracker Records) Another Australian pick, this time on the Firecracker sub label Unthank that has the most beautiful screen printed covers like its parent label. Kagami Smile - Thigh (BLCR Laboratories) From the creepy surreal Shintaro Kago-esque artwork to the hi-fi granular rhythms and sounds, this album is really a fantastic listen. Much more laidback than Kagami Smile's typical sound, this felt more focused and utilized chaotic ideas in a more structured way. It'll please anybody looking for more organic sounds congealed around the skeleton of a contemporary beat-driven piece. FIRE-TOOLZ - INTERBEING (Bedlam Tapes) Combing my two loves, Industrial music and vaporwave, into a lovely mess of vapornoise textures, FIRE-TOOLZ hits back with yet another flamethrower. I greatly admire her curation with Swamp Circle records but her sound is near-unmatched in the (imo) under-appreciated subgenre of vaporwave. Pharmakon - Contact (Sacred Bones) One of the most powerful presences in the industrial and harsh noise scenes, Pharmakon never fails to please with her screeching steel and unhindered ferocity. This record is just so vicious, with its sheer hatred burning through just as strong as ever. ZONΞ ΞATΞR vs. §E▲ ▓F D▓G§ (Chamber38) This is probably the most insane mixture of sampled industrial and noise metal I've ever heard. Like a thousand saw blades in a vortex of distorted guitars, blast beats, death growls, power electronics. The list goes one, but its safe to say this masterpiece is a fantastic aural cleanser. Tee Lopes - Sonic Mania OST (Data Discs) What else can I say that hasn't already been established? The Sonic franchise has the best music and its just as good as ever with the addition of new classics like Studiopolis and Press Garden. LEUCROCUTA - when all the animals are dead (self-release) A jarring and beautiful soundtrack to the sci-fi dystopic world beyond nature. The concept is strong enough alone, but the music holds up just as well, pressing some lovely synth-waves sounds harshened by the banshee-esque shrieked vocal performance that adds a fantastic spice to the dissonant danceable sounds. VRTUA - LOUD FORMATIONS (Beer on the Rug) That Yamaha chip is just the most unbeatable sound around. FM was damn near perfected by the Sega Genesis' sound engine and this masterpiece is living proof. Using the sounds from said chip, VTRUA harnesses the limitations to breed this fantastic showcase of what you can do marrying todays techniques with yesterday's killer sounds. RELEASES :

Phi-Psonics - Expanding to One (Gondwana Records)

Definitely my favorite album of the year. Came across this one a few weeks ago, and been playing it on loop since then. It just felt so soothing to have my mind wander while listening to it alone at night. The perfect balance between (non-boring) jazz and new age, with a delicate way of blending western and non-western music.

Brìghde Chaimbeul - Sunwise

I’ve been to her concert in Lyon this fall and the moment was so solemn and fulfilling. The album is exactly the same. A pure voice coupled with entrancing small pipes, oscillating between drone stasis and folk take-offs.

V/A – Remanences (Ghost Dance)

Great V/A from Marseille-based Ghost Dance. Hats off to my dear friend Brahim Lumière (who runs the label) for bringing such a vaporous aesthetics through this heterogeneous compilation. Bonus: I’m super happy that it includes an edit of mine.

Lucien Balconi – Pierre ☆ Feuille ☆ Ciseaux (Transatlantic)

Amongst the wide sea of ethereal releases we have these days, this one has something more. First, epic and sad electric guitars, just like I love them. Then, a lot of folk-rock ballads, just like I love them.

John Maus – Later Than You Think (Young)

Another album I’ve been listening to on loop. I went to his concerts twice this year, and each time was awesome, thanks to John Maus’ crazy performance. As always, his formula seems pretty simple, but it’s so effective and catchy, I can’t get the lyrics nor the melodies out of my mind.

Flower B – Locked-In (Big Science)

This album is such a blast, every time I give it a listen I am amazed by the complexity of the tracks, and the sound design is so HD while the music feels so nasty, ghettoish and powerful. 8 tracks = 8 ultimate bangers.

Raisa K – Affectionately (15 love)

Cool release from the London-based producer on 15 love (I’ll always be thankful to them for releasing ML Buch). Great vocals on an indus and indie trip-pop vibe, with a recurrent melodic theme coming back throughout the album.

SOS_CARLOSS – SICH VERSTEHEN (LAYE AUDIO)

Here’s some heavy leftfield bass, digital dancehall both fitting the dancefloor and the listening sessions. Just repetitive enough to be hypnotic, half-tempo broken quality rhythms and a dreamy overall atmosphere that sometimes reminds me of the first releases of Canadian RAMZi on Pygmy Animals.

Jonquera & Officium - Ambient Nash Recordings & Friends (Teenage Menopause)

Another couple of friends in this list. I loved their album, but definitely added them here for their live act I attended to, which won over the whole audience. I’m sure everyone would have enjoyed for this hour of psychedelic rock’n’blues to last the whole night. Maybe we should have recorded the concert with a VCR, and then played it again and again on a rusty cathode ray tube screen, including a lot of VHS grain.

MIXES:

Living Room n°83 ~ DJ In A Dream

Beautiful, poetic, dreamy. To be listened at night. Coming back to it on a regular basis. My favorite mix of 2025.

NTS Guide to: Ambient Americana Vol. III

At last, I could feel again like when I first heard the “Sad cowboys and the sound of rain” mix by Daniel Rincon. Now, I wanna go back to Red Dead Redemption 2 beautiful lands.

LYL RADIO - Free the Jo with Force Feedback

InnerMost /////////////////

Old Saw - The Wringing Cloth (Lobby Art)

"Having moved away from New England a few years ago, this album really brought me home. Old Saw has this way of capturing the area in which I grew up with such vivid detail - something beyond the sum of its parts. A pondside wearing wintergreen, hornet nests in an abandoned sawmill, firework remains scattered across the sandpit. In this way, The Wringing Cloth makes for an album very close to my heart." - Simon

TKB - 888 - 890 (world of knots)

"I spent a few days in the late fall helping to build a house at a farm in a valley a few hours north of Reykjavík. Completely alone out there on the hillside for long stretches, at one point as the sun was setting I decided to throw this one on. In that liminal space between day and night I was suddenly overcome by the feeling of being observed, like some presence in the hills was keeping an eye on me. I get the impression this album really invites something supernatural to our physical realm." - Simon

Albert - Return to Sender (J. Albert Productions) Bamboo Shows ///// /////// /////// RELEASES : Phi-Psonics - Expanding to One (Gondwana Records) Definitely my favorite album of the year. Came across this one a few weeks ago, and been playing it on loop since then. It just felt so soothing to have my mind wander while listening to it alone at night. The perfect balance between (non-boring) jazz and new age, with a delicate way of blending western and non-western music. Brìghde Chaimbeul - Sunwise I’ve been to her concert in Lyon this fall and the moment was so solemn and fulfilling. The album is exactly the same. A pure voice coupled with entrancing small pipes, oscillating between drone stasis and folk take-offs. V/A – Remanences (Ghost Dance) Great V/A from Marseille-based Ghost Dance. Hats off to my dear friend Brahim Lumière (who runs the label) for bringing such a vaporous aesthetics through this heterogeneous compilation. Bonus: I’m super happy that it includes an edit of mine. Lucien Balconi – Pierre ☆ Feuille ☆ Ciseaux (Transatlantic) Amongst the wide sea of ethereal releases we have these days, this one has something more. First, epic and sad electric guitars, just like I love them. Then, a lot of folk-rock ballads, just like I love them. John Maus – Later Than You Think (Young) Another album I’ve been listening to on loop. I went to his concerts twice this year, and each time was awesome, thanks to John Maus’ crazy performance. As always, his formula seems pretty simple, but it’s so effective and catchy, I can’t get the lyrics nor the melodies out of my mind. Flower B – Locked-In (Big Science) This album is such a blast, every time I give it a listen I am amazed by the complexity of the tracks, and the sound design is so HD while the music feels so nasty, ghettoish and powerful. 8 tracks = 8 ultimate bangers. Raisa K – Affectionately (15 love) Cool release from the London-based producer on 15 love (I’ll always be thankful to them for releasing ML Buch). Great vocals on an indus and indie trip-pop vibe, with a recurrent melodic theme coming back throughout the album. SOS_CARLOSS – SICH VERSTEHEN (LAYE AUDIO) Here’s some heavy leftfield bass, digital dancehall both fitting the dancefloor and the listening sessions. Just repetitive enough to be hypnotic, half-tempo broken quality rhythms and a dreamy overall atmosphere that sometimes reminds me of the first releases of Canadian RAMZi on Pygmy Animals. Jonquera & Officium - Ambient Nash Recordings & Friends (Teenage Menopause) Another couple of friends in this list. I loved their album, but definitely added them here for their live act I attended to, which won over the whole audience. I’m sure everyone would have enjoyed for this hour of psychedelic rock’n’blues to last the whole night. Maybe we should have recorded the concert with a VCR, and then played it again and again on a rusty cathode ray tube screen, including a lot of VHS grain. MIXES: Living Room n°83 ~ DJ In A Dream Beautiful, poetic, dreamy. To be listened at night. Coming back to it on a regular basis. My favorite mix of 2025. NTS Guide to: Ambient Americana Vol. III At last, I could feel again like when I first heard the “Sad cowboys and the sound of rain” mix by Daniel Rincon. Now, I wanna go back to Red Dead Redemption 2 beautiful lands. LYL RADIO - Free the Jo with Force Feedback To be listened LOUD while driving really fast at the countryside. Crazy jungle, always getting stronger.
